Specify a Reference Model for Sample Size Calculations

Source: R/pmgen_reference.R
pmgen_reference.Rd

Constructs a reference logistic regression model by finding the intercept and coefficient scalar that jointly achieve a target prevalence and c-statistic in the joint predictor distribution. The unit Fisher information matrix is also computed and stored in the returned object.

Usage

pmgen_reference(
  joint_data,
  predictors = NULL,
  coef = NULL,
  bisection = TRUE,
  bisection_method = c("independent", "mvn"),
  intercept = NULL,
  prevalence = NULL,
  cstatistic = NULL,
  tolerance = 0.001,
  n_bisect_pop = 1e+06,
  n_synth = 1e+06,
  max_iter = 100,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

joint_data

A data frame (one row per individual, columns = predictors) representing the joint predictor distribution. Alternatively, a named list of distributional assumptions (see Details). Required.

predictors

Character vector of predictor column names to use from joint_data. If NULL, all columns of joint_data are used (when joint_data is a data frame).

coef

Named numeric vector of predictor coefficients. Names must match predictors. Meaning depends on bisection: when bisection = TRUE, these are relative weights (on the log-odds scale, before scaling) — if NULL, all predictors are given equal weight of 1. When bisection = FALSE, these are the final coefficients used directly (no default; must be supplied).

bisection

Logical. If TRUE (default), run the two-step bisection procedure to calibrate coef/intercept against prevalence/ cstatistic. If FALSE, bypass bisection entirely and use the supplied intercept/coef directly as the reference model — useful when a reference model has already been fully specified elsewhere (e.g. from the literature) and bisection-based calibration is not wanted.

bisection_method

One of "independent" (default) or "mvn". Only used when bisection = TRUE and joint_data is a data frame. "independent" calibrates against a synthetic population generated by fitting independent marginal distributions to joint_data (fast, but discards correlation between predictors). "mvn" instead calibrates against a synthetic population drawn from a multivariate normal approximation to joint_data that preserves its correlation structure (binary columns are dichotomized after generation); see Details. "mvn" is not supported when joint_data is a distributional- assumptions list (predictors are already independent there by construction).

intercept

Numeric scalar. Required when bisection = FALSE; ignored when bisection = TRUE (the intercept is instead solved for by the inner bisection).

prevalence

Target outcome prevalence (0, 1). Required when bisection = TRUE. Optional when bisection = FALSE — if supplied, the achieved prevalence is compared to it for informational reporting only.

cstatistic

Target c-statistic (AUC), must be > 0.5. Required when bisection = TRUE. Optional when bisection = FALSE — if supplied, the achieved c-statistic is compared to it for informational reporting only.

tolerance

Convergence tolerance for both bisection procedures. Default 0.001. Unused when bisection = FALSE.

n_bisect_pop

Integer. Size of the super-population used internally during bisection. Larger values give more stable estimates but are slower. Default 1e6. Unused when bisection = FALSE.

n_synth

Integer. When joint_data is a distributional-assumptions list, the number of synthetic individuals to generate. Default 1e6.

max_iter

Integer. Maximum bisection iterations. Default 100. Unused when bisection = FALSE.

seed

Integer or NULL. Random seed for reproducibility.

Value

A pmgen_ref_model object with components: coef, intercept, prevalence_achieved, cstat_achieved, predictors, joint_data, unit_info_matrix, inv_unit_info.

Details

Supplying a dataset (joint_data as a data frame): The data frame is used directly as the super-population for bisection and for computing the unit information matrix. This is the recommended approach when synthetic or real pilot data are available.

Supplying distributional assumptions (joint_data as a named list): Each list element specifies the marginal distribution of one predictor: list(dist = "normal", mean = 50, sd = 10) or list(dist = "bernoulli", prob = 0.3). Predictors are assumed independent. A synthetic population of n_synth rows is generated before bisection.

The bisection procedure follows Austin's two-step approach:

  1. Inner bisection (intercept): for a fixed scalar s, find the intercept b0 such that mean(plogis(b0 + s * X %*% coef)) = prevalence.

  2. Outer bisection (scalar): find s such that the c-statistic of the resulting model in the super-population equals cstatistic.

Bypassing bisection (bisection = FALSE): supply intercept and coef directly as the final reference model. This is useful when the reference model's coefficients are already known (e.g. published in the literature) and bisecting against a synthetic population derived from joint_data is undesirable — for instance, because it would assume predictor independence when joint_data is a data frame (see .fit_marginals()). The unit information matrix is still computed from joint_data as usual.

Correlation-preserving bisection (bisection_method = "mvn"): when joint_data is a data frame with correlated predictors, calibrating against a synthetic population that assumes independence (the default "independent" method) can distort the calibrated reference model. The "mvn" method instead estimates a multivariate normal approximation to joint_data (means, SDs, and the full correlation matrix, via cor()) and analytically solves for the linear predictor's mean and variance needed to hit the target prevalence/cstatistic (assuming a normal linear predictor), then rescales coef so the resulting predictor combination has that variance. Binary (0/1) columns are generated as normal and then dichotomized to match their empirical proportion; this mildly attenuates their correlation with other predictors relative to the input correlation matrix (no correction is applied for this).

Note that bisection without coef gives every predictor the same coefficient. If the predictors' true effects differ (in size or sign), this equal-weights model can give noticeably different simulation results (e.g. a different expected calibration slope at small N) from the true model; supply coef (relative weights) where they are known.

References

Riley RD, Whittle R, Sadatsafavi M, Martin GP, Pate A, Collins GS, Ensor J. A general sample size framework for developing or updating a predictive algorithm: with application to clinical prediction models. BMC Medical Research Methodology. 2026;26:121. doi:10.1186/s12874-026-02856-7

Examples

# n_bisect_pop and n_synth are reduced from their defaults (1e6) so that
# the examples run quickly; use the defaults in practice.

# From a supplied dataset (equal relative weights for all predictors)
predictors <- setdiff(names(dvt_data), "dvt")
ref <- pmgen_reference(
  joint_data   = dvt_data,
  predictors   = predictors,
  prevalence   = 0.21,
  cstatistic   = 0.78,
  n_bisect_pop = 1e5,
  n_synth      = 1e5,
  seed         = 42
)
#> Running bisection to calibrate reference model...
#> Bisection converged: prevalence=0.2100 (target=0.2100), c-stat=0.7791 (target=0.7800)
#> Unit information matrix computed and cached.
ref
#> pmgen reference model
#> ---------------------
#>   Predictors        : male, OCuse, malignancy, surgery, ab_leg_trauma, vein_distension, calf_diff, ab_ddimer, pregnancy, immobile, clotting
#>   Intercept         : -4.7089
#>   Prevalence (achieved): 0.2100
#>   C-statistic (achieved): 0.7791
#>   Coefficients      :
#>            male           OCuse      malignancy         surgery   ab_leg_trauma 
#>          0.9375          0.9375          0.9375          0.9375          0.9375 
#> vein_distension       calf_diff       ab_ddimer       pregnancy        immobile 
#>          0.9375          0.9375          0.9375          0.9375          0.9375 
#>        clotting 
#>          0.9375 
#>   Unit info matrix  : cached (12x12)

# From distributional assumptions
ref_dist <- pmgen_reference(
  joint_data = list(
    age  = list(dist = "normal",    mean = 0, sd = 1),
    bp   = list(dist = "normal",    mean = 0, sd = 1),
    hist = list(dist = "bernoulli", prob = 0.3)
  ),
  prevalence   = 0.10,
  cstatistic   = 0.75,
  n_bisect_pop = 1e5,
  n_synth      = 1e5,
  seed         = 42
)
#> Running bisection to calibrate reference model...
#> Bisection converged: prevalence=0.1000 (target=0.1000), c-stat=0.7491 (target=0.7500)
#> Unit information matrix computed and cached.

# Bypassing bisection with a fully pre-specified reference model
ref_fixed <- pmgen_reference(
  joint_data = dvt_data,
  predictors = c("malignancy", "calf_diff", "ab_ddimer"),
  bisection  = FALSE,
  intercept  = -2.5,
  coef       = c(malignancy = 0.5, calf_diff = 0.8, ab_ddimer = 1.5),
  n_synth    = 1e5,
  seed       = 42
)
#> Using supplied reference model (bisection bypassed): prevalence=0.2541, c-stat=0.7068
#> Unit information matrix computed and cached.
